# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: OSC colour queries, sets and resets (OSC 4, 10, 11, 12, 104, 110, 111, 112)   (issue #10 part 2, wave 8)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/osc_color_spec.txt   (spec-researcher output, 2026-10-31)
# Companion: reports_spec.txt (the reply path, DA/DSR/..., same table format) and reports_spec.notes.md.
#
# FORMAT (one table-driven test, tests/osc_color.rs, through common::check_table; every failing id is reported;
# each row also runs with the bytes split at every offset (Chunking))
#   ### ID / size: RxC / step: feed <bytes> / reply: <bytes>|none / cite: / note: / flags:   as reports_spec.txt.
#         \x07 is BEL. `reply:` is the concatenation of every Request::Reply since the previous `reply:` (or the start).
#   step: set size <R>x<C>   Terminal::resize(rows, cols) (the grid size of the row changes; overrides must survive).
#   step: set theme <spec>   Terminal::set_theme_colors(ThemeColors{..}); <spec> is `T` (the TEST THEME below) or `T2` (the second
#                            theme below). Rows without it use T.
#   expect: <k>=<#rrggbb> .. the EFFECTIVE colours (theme + overrides) after the steps above it. k = fg | bg | cursor | pal[N].
#                            Checked against the Terminal colour API (the exact accessor names are the implementer's).
#   overrides: <list>|none   the keys with a program override (Terminal::color_overrides()), as `fg bg cursor pal[1] pal[7]`,
#                            in that order (fg, bg, cursor, then palette ascending); `none` = empty.
#   gen: +1 | same           colors_generation() relative to its value at the previous `gen:` line (or the row start):
#                            `+1` means "increased" (any increase counts), `same` unchanged. "bumps on any effective change".
#   cite/flags               as reports_spec.txt: decision | xterm-quirk | negative | unverified | security | control
#
# TEST THEME T (synthetic, so a wrong index shows at once)           fg #d0d0d0   bg #101010   cursor #ffcc00
#     palette[i] = ( i , 255 - i , i XOR 0x55 )  for i in 0..=255      e.g. pal[0]=#00ff55 pal[1]=#01fe54 pal[2]=#02fd57
#     pal[7]=#07f852 pal[15]=#0ff05a pal[16]=#10ef45 pal[100]=#649b31 pal[200]=#c8379d pal[255]=#ff00aa
# TEST THEME T2                                                      fg #aabbcc   bg #223344   cursor #00ff00
#     palette[i] = ( 255 - i , i , i XOR 0xaa )
#     pal[1]=#fe01ab pal[2]=#fd02a8
#
# PRIMARY SOURCES (fetched 2026-10-31)
#   [CTL]  xterm ctlseqs https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.txt, section "Operating System Commands":
#          "XTerm accepts either BEL or ST for terminating OSC sequences, and when returning information, uses the same terminator
#          used in a query." "If a ? is given rather than a name or RGB specification, xterm replies with a control sequence of the
#          same form which can be used to set the corresponding color ... Because more than one pair of color number and specification
#          can be given in one control sequence, xterm can make more than one reply." "Ps = 104 ; c -> Reset Color Number c ... If no
#          parameters are given, the entire table will be reset." "Ps = 110 -> Reset VT100 text foreground color. 111 background,
#          112 text cursor color." "Each successive parameter changes the next color in the list. The value of Ps tells the starting
#          point in the list." (the 10;a;b chain)
#   [XT]   xterm source (ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots master, XTERM_PATCH 412, as fetched 2026-10-31):
#            misc.c L4000..4180 do_osc (number parse, `final` = the query's terminator echoed), L2636..2659 ReportAnsiColorRequest
#            (`"%d;%d;rgb:%04x/%04x/%04x"`, lowercase), L2980..3010 ChangeAnsiColorRequest (loop: atoi index, `?` queries, first error
#            breaks the loop), L3130.. ResetAnsiColorRequest (104), L3568..3600 ReportColorRequest (`"%d;rgb:%04x/%04x/%04x"`, Ps = 10 + i),
#            L3662..3715 ChangeColorsRequest (chain: i = start..; an empty piece (`;;`) skips one colour), L3718..3750 ResetColorsRequest;
#            do_osc: `!need_data && !optional_data` -> a 110..119 with data is ignored; 104/105 take optional data;
#            charproc.c L14358..14412 ReallyReset: the COMMON part (DECSTR and RIS alike) calls reset_SGR_Colors and
#            ResetAnsiColorRequest(all) -> xterm resets the 256-colour palette on DECSTR AND RIS; it never resets the dynamic colours
#            (10/11/12) in either; the RIS-only block does not touch colours either.
#   [XL]   X Window System "Color Strings": rgb:<r>/<g>/<b> with 1..4 hex digits per channel, SCALED (f -> ffff); "#rgb" .. "#rrrrggggbbbb"
#          with equal 1..4 digit groups, LEFT-JUSTIFIED (the leading digits are the most significant bits: #3a7 == #3000a0007000, so
#          #fff is 0xf0f0f0, not white); rgbi:<f>/<f>/<f> floats 0..1; names from rgb.txt (case/space-insensitive); CIE specs.
#   [VT]   neovim tui.c L350..353: `ESC ] 11 ; ? BEL` immediately followed by `ESC [ 5 n` (the DSR 5 reply is the "no answer to the
#          colour query" sentinel; the colour answer, when there is one, arrives first); neovim parses the reply
#          `OSC 11 ; rgb:rrrr/gggg/bbbb` terminated by BEL or ST. fish terminal.rs L323: `ESC ] 11 ; ? ESC \` (ST!) after `ESC [ 0 c`
#          (DA1), `ESC [ > 0 q` (XTVERSION), `ESC [ ? u`, `ESC [ 6 n`; fish also enables `CSI ? 2031 h` (colour theme reporting).
#          tmux queries OSC 10 / OSC 11 (tty.c, `\033]10;?\033\\` and `\033]11;?\033\\`) and parses `rgb:` replies (tty-keys.c).
#   [KT]   kitty https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/ (escape code docs "Colors" and the dynamic colours: OSC 4/10/11/12 query replies in
#          `rgb:rrrr/gggg/bbbb`, terminator echoed; RIS resets dynamic colours; DECSTR does not). From memory of kitty/colors.c and
#          screen.c, not re-fetched in this run: marked "(from memory)".
#   [WZ] [GH] [AL] [IT]  WezTerm, Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2: only "(from memory)" statements; none re-fetched. RIS resets the colours
#          in Alacritty (`reset_state`), WezTerm (full reset) and Ghostty; DECSTR does not touch colours in any of them.
#
# DECISIONS (D-xxx; lead confirms; the rows follow the recommendation):
#   D-REPLY     A query reply is `OSC <n> ; rgb:RRRR/GGGG/BBBB <T>` for 10/11/12 (n = 10/11/12) and `OSC 4 ; <idx> ; rgb:RRRR/GGGG/BBBB <T>`
#               for the palette: lowercase hex, 4 digits per channel = the 8-bit value * 257 (0xd0 -> d0d0), 7-bit OSC introducer (ESC ]),
#               <T> = BEL if the query ended with BEL, ESC \ otherwise (ST, 8-bit ST, CAN/SUB/ESC-aborted: all give ESC \ because the
#               parser reports only "bell terminated" yes/no). Replies come out through reply_osc (7-bit) in query order.
#   D-VTBELL    PREREQUISITE (scope amendment for the brief): tessera-vt's Action::Osc drops vte's `bell_terminated` (lib.rs L278
#               `_bell_terminated`), so the terminal cannot echo the terminator today. The implementer must add the flag to Action::Osc
#               (or a sibling) and update the OSC callers; ADR 0022's "the terminator is not visible" note changes with it.
#   D-QUERY     A `?` answers only for the colours Tessera has: 4 (index 0..=255), 10, 11, 12. The chain 10;?;? answers 10 then 11
#               (xterm); 11;?;? answers 11 then 12; 12;?;? answers 12 only (13 = pointer colour does not exist here). A piece that is
#               neither `?` nor a valid spec leaves that colour alone (xterm) and later pieces still apply to later colours.
#   D-SPEC      Accepted set specs (case-insensitive prefix/hex): `rgb:` with 1..4 hex digits per channel scaled to 8 bits by
#               v * 255 / (16^n - 1) truncated through the 16-bit value (xterm), i.e. high byte of v * 65535 / (16^n - 1);
#               `#` + 3, 6, 9 or 12 hex digits (see D-HASH). Rejected (ignored whole): everything else, including `rgbi:`, `CIE*:`,
#               `rgb(...)`, names (D-NAMES), empty, surrounding blanks, a sign, fewer/more digits, mixed digit counts, non-hex.
#   D-HASH      LEAD DECISION 2026-10-31: xterm/Xlib [XL] semantics. Each group is LEFT-JUSTIFIED (#f00 = #f00000; #f80 = #f08000),
#               not CSS nibble doubling (kitty/WezTerm/Alacritty). 6 digits: as is. 9 and 12 digits: the top 8 bits of each group
#               (#123456789 = #124578). Row OS-HASH3 follows this.
#   D-NAMES     X11 colour names are NOT accepted in this task (ignored whole). X11 and CSS names disagree (gray 190 vs 128, green 0,255,0
#               vs 0,128,0, maroon, purple), and a 750-entry table is a separate issue. xterm, kitty and Ghostty accept names, WezTerm
#               (CSS names) too: file a follow-up; rows OS-NAME* flip then.
#   D-STOP4     OSC 4 / 104 processing stops at the first malformed pair/index (xterm `break`): earlier pairs stay applied, later ones are
#               not. An index >= 256 is malformed. (kitty skips and continues, from memory.)
#   D-OSC4-IDX  The index is decimal digits only (1..3 chars after trimming no whitespace): `+1`, `1x`, ``, `-1`, `0x10` are malformed
#               (xterm's atoi accepts `1x` as 1 and `` as 0: quirks Tessera does not copy). Leading zeros are fine (`001`).
#   D-RESET     RIS drops EVERY override (palette and dynamic) and bumps the generation if any effective colour changed; DECSTR and DECSCL
#               keep every override (the `// #10` question in soft_reset). xterm resets the palette on both and keeps the dynamic colours
#               on both; kitty/Alacritty/WezTerm/Ghostty follow the Tessera rule (from memory). NEEDS THE LEAD (brief says "DECSTR per
#               fixture"). Alternate-screen switches, resize and the title stack never touch colours.
#   D-THEME-KEEP A theme change updates the defaults; overrides stay (the brief's D-THEME-KEEP) and are reported by queries; reset
#               (104/110-112/RIS) falls back to the NEW theme. Setting an override equal to the current effective colour still records it.
#   D-GEN       colors_generation() increases exactly when some EFFECTIVE colour changed (set to a different value, reset of an
#               override whose value differs from the theme, theme change that alters an un-overridden colour, RIS dropping a differing
#               override); a no-op never bumps it.
#   D-REVERSE   DECSCNM (?5) does not swap the reported colours (xterm reports the opposite colour; kitty, Alacritty do not).
#   D-SELECT    OSC 17/19 (selection colours), 5/105 (special colours) and 13..16/18 stay ignored (brief: out of scope), also as chain
#               members: the chain stops at 12.
#   D-PIECES    tessera-vt cuts an OSC after 16 pieces without a flag (ADR 0022 D-PARAMS): `4;..` with more than 7 pairs applies/answers
#               the first 7 only. Unpaired trailing pieces are ignored.
# =============================================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ OQ. Queries

### OQ01_osc11_query_bel
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;?\x07
reply: \e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\x07
cite: [CTL] reply "uses the same terminator used in a query"; [XT] ReportColorRequest `%d;rgb:%04x/%04x/%04x` with 10 + index; D-REPLY (bg #101010 -> 1010)
flags: control

### OQ02_osc11_query_st
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;?\e\\
reply: \e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\e\\
cite: [CTL]; [VT] fish terminal.rs L323 sends the ST form
flags: control

### OQ03_osc10_query
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]10;?\x07\e]10;?\e\\
reply: \e]10;rgb:d0d0/d0d0/d0d0\x07\e]10;rgb:d0d0/d0d0/d0d0\e\\
cite: [XT] ReportColorRequest for the text foreground; tmux sends the ST form (tty.c), others BEL
flags: control

### OQ04_osc12_query
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]12;?\x07\e]12;?\e\\
reply: \e]12;rgb:ffff/cccc/0000\x07\e]12;rgb:ffff/cccc/0000\e\\
cite: [XT] text cursor colour is index 12; theme cursor #ffcc00 -> ffff/cccc/0000
flags: control

### OQ05_osc4_query_each_terminator
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;?\x07\e]4;1;?\e\\
reply: \e]4;1;rgb:0101/fefe/5454\x07\e]4;1;rgb:0101/fefe/5454\e\\
cite: [XT] ReportAnsiColorRequest `%d;%d;rgb:%04x/%04x/%04x` (opcode 4, index); pal[1] = #01fe54
flags: control

### OQ06_osc4_query_edges
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;0;?\x07\e]4;15;?\x07\e]4;16;?\x07\e]4;100;?\x07\e]4;200;?\x07\e]4;255;?\x07
reply: \e]4;0;rgb:0000/ffff/5555\x07\e]4;15;rgb:0f0f/f0f0/5a5a\x07\e]4;16;rgb:1010/efef/4545\x07\e]4;100;rgb:6464/9b9b/3131\x07\e]4;200;rgb:c8c8/3737/9d9d\x07\e]4;255;rgb:ffff/0000/aaaa\x07
cite: [XT] first, last and middle indexes of the 256-colour table; ADR/brief: palette is 256 entries
flags: control

### OQ07_osc4_two_queries_two_replies
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;?;2;?\x07
reply: \e]4;1;rgb:0101/fefe/5454\x07\e]4;2;rgb:0202/fdfd/5757\x07
cite: [CTL] "xterm can make more than one reply"; [XT] ChangeAnsiColorRequest loop; each reply carries the terminator (final) of the query
flags: control

### OQ08_osc4_mixed_set_and_query_in_order
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;?;2;rgb:ff/00/00;3;?\e\\
reply: \e]4;1;rgb:0101/fefe/5454\e\\\e]4;3;rgb:0303/fcfc/5656\e\\
expect: pal[2]=#ff0000
overrides: pal[2]
cite: [XT] pairs are processed left to right; the set in the middle produces no reply
flags: control

### OQ09_osc4_set_then_query_same_osc
size: 24x80

reply: \e]4;1;rgb:1010/2020/3030\x07
cite: [XT] ChangeAnsiColorRequest applies pair 1 before reading pair 2
flags: control

size: 24x80

cite: D-QUERY / D-SELECT: xterm would go on to 13 (pointer fg) and 14; Tessera has no pointer colours, so the chain ends at 12

### OQ15_chain_empty_piece_skips_one_colour
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]10;;#445566\x07
reply: none
expect: fg=#d0d0d0 bg=#445566
overrides: bg
cite: [XT] ChangeColorsRequest: `names[0] == ';'` -> thisName = NULL, the colour is skipped and the next piece goes to the next colour
flags: xterm-quirk

### OQ16_query_after_set_roundtrip
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;#ff8000\x07\e]11;?\x07
reply: \e]11;rgb:ffff/8080/0000\x07
expect: bg=#ff8000
cite: [XT] the reply is the 16-bit value the server holds; 8-bit 0x80 -> 8080; D-REPLY
flags: control

### OQ17_query_survives_dec_reverse_video
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[?5h\e]11;?\x07\e]10;?\x07
reply: \e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\x07\e]10;rgb:d0d0/d0d0/d0d0\x07
cite: D-REVERSE: [XT] ReportColorRequest reports the opposite colour under reverse video (`oppositeColor`); kitty and Alacritty (from memory) do not swap
flags: decision xterm-quirk

### OQ18_query_uppercase_hex_never_in_reply
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;7;#ABCDEF\x07\e]4;7;?\x07

cite: [XT] `%04x` lowercase
flags: control

### OQ19_query_with_trailing_garbage_ignored
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;?x\x07\e]11;? \x07\e]11;??\x07\e]11;?;\x07
reply: \e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\x07
cite: [XT] `strcmp(thisName, "?")`: only exactly `?` queries; `?x`, `? `, `??` are specs and fail to parse. The last form `11;?;` is a query followed by an empty piece for 12 (xterm: nothing more), so ONE reply
flags: xterm-quirk

### OQ20_queries_20_and_up_are_silent
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]13;?\x07\e]14;?\x07\e]15;?\x07\e]16;?\x07\e]17;?\x07\e]18;?\x07\e]19;?\x07\e]5;0;?\x07\e]105;0\x07
reply: none
cite: D-SELECT (the brief puts 17/19 and 5/105 out of scope; xterm answers 13..19 and 5)
flags: decision negative

### OQ21_neovim_bg_query_then_dsr
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;?\x07\e[5n
reply: \e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\x07\e[0n
cite: [VT] neovim tui.c L353: the colour answer arrives first, the DSR 5 reply after it, in that order (D-ORDER of reports_spec.txt); BEL echoed because the query used BEL
flags: control

### OQ22_fish_startup_burst
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[?u\e[0c\e[>0q\e[6n\e]11;?\e\\

cite: [VT] fish terminal.rs L171..L323 (kitty keyboard query, DA1 as `CSI 0 c`, XTVERSION `CSI > 0 q`, CPR, OSC 11 with ST); every reply present and in order; <VERSION> as in reports_spec.txt

flags: control

### OQ24_osc_aborted_by_esc_still_replies_with_st
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;?\e[6n
reply: \e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\e\\\e[1;1R
cite: ADR 0022 D-CAN: ESC ends the OSC and dispatches what was collected (xterm discards it); the ESC is not a BEL, so ST is echoed; then `ESC [ 6 n` is a CPR. Consequence of the parser (D-VTBELL), recorded as a decision
flags: decision xterm-quirk

### OQ25_osc_aborted_by_can_replies
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;?\x18\e]11;?\x1a
reply: \e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\e\\\e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\e\\
cite: ADR 0022 D-CAN as OQ24 (CAN and SUB dispatch the collected OSC)
flags: decision xterm-quirk

### OQ26_8bit_st_terminator_replies_st
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;?\u{9c}
reply: none
cite: unverified: U+009C is encoded C2 9C in the UTF-8 stream; tessera-vt (vte, UTF-8 input) does not treat it as ST, so the OSC stays open and nothing is answered until a real terminator. A raw 0x9C byte is invalid UTF-8
flags: unverified negative

### OQ27_osc4_reply_for_eight_pairs_is_cut_at_seven
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]4;1;?;2;?;3;?;4;?;5;?;6;?;7;?;8;?\x07
reply: \e]4;1;rgb:0101/fefe/5454\x07\e]4;2;rgb:0202/fdfd/5757\x07\e]4;3;rgb:0303/fcfc/5656\x07\e]4;4;rgb:0404/fbfb/5151\x07\e]4;5;rgb:0505/fafa/5050\x07\e]4;6;rgb:0606/f9f9/5353\x07\e]4;7;rgb:0707/f8f8/5252\x07
cite: D-PIECES: the parser keeps 16 pieces (`4` + 7 pairs = 15 pieces; the 16th piece `8` is an unpaired index and is ignored, the 8th `?` is cut). xterm answers all eight. Recorded so the limit is visible
flags: decision xterm-quirk

### OQ28_query_inside_alt_screen_same_colours
size: 24x80
step: feed \e[?1049h\e]11;?\x07
reply: \e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\x07
cite: D-RESET: colours belong to the terminal, not to a screen
flags: control

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ OS. Sets: accepted specs

### OS01_rgb_two_digits
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;rgb:ff/80/00\x07
expect: bg=#ff8000
overrides: bg
gen: +1
cite: [XL] rgb: scaled; [XT] AllocateTermColor via XParseColor
flags: control

### OS02_rgb_one_digit_scaled
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;rgb:f/8/0\x07\e]11;?\x07
reply: \e]11;rgb:ffff/8888/0000\x07
expect: bg=#ff8800
cite: [XL] rgb:f -> ffff (scaled, not left-justified); 8 -> 8888 -> high byte 88
flags: control

### OS03_rgb_three_digits_scaled
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;rgb:fff/000/800\x07
expect: bg=#ff0080
cite: [XL] 3 digits: v * 65535 / 4095; 0x800 -> 0x8008 -> 0x80; D-SPEC
flags: control

### OS04_rgb_three_digits_mixed
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;rgb:123/456/789\x07
expect: bg=#124578
cite: [XL] 0x123 -> 0x1230 -> 12; 0x456 -> 0x4562 -> 45; 0x789 -> 0x7898 -> 78
flags: control

### OS05_rgb_four_digits_high_byte
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;rgb:1234/5678/9abc\x07
expect: bg=#12569a
cite: [XL] 16-bit channel -> high byte (truncation, as an X server maps to a 24-bit visual); D-SPEC
flags: decision

### OS06_rgb_four_digits_rounding_ambiguity
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;rgb:9abc/9abc/9abc\x07
expect: bg=#9a9a9a
cite: 0x9abc/257 = 154.7: truncation gives 0x9a, rounding 0x9b. Pinned to truncation (xterm); kitty may round (from memory)
flags: decision unverified

### OS07_rgb_prefix_case_insensitive
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;RGB:FF/00/00\x07
expect: bg=#ff0000
cite: [XL] the colour-space prefix is case-insensitive; hex digits any case
flags: unverified

### OS08_hash_six_digits
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;#ff8000\x07
expect: bg=#ff8000
cite: [XL] #rrggbb; [CTL]
flags: control

### OS-HASH3_hash_three_digits_left_justified
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;#f80\x07
expect: bg=#f08000
cite: D-HASH (lead decision 2026-10-31): [XL]/xterm left-justified, f000/8000/0000 -> f0,80,00. kitty/WezTerm/Alacritty would give #ff8800 (CSS doubling, from memory)
flags: decision

### OS10_hash_nine_digits_high_byte

### OI04_hash_bad_lengths
size: 24x80

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ OT. Theme interaction (D-THEME-KEEP)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ OZ. Limits and security

### OZ01_flood_of_queries
size: 24x80
step: feed (1,000,000 times) \e]4;1;?\x07
cite: the terminal queues 1,000,000 replies; the bound is app-core's outbox (reports_spec RP09). The test checks the first and last reply and linear time. Generated by the test
flags: security

### OZ02_flood_of_sets_bounded_state
size: 24x80
step: feed (1,000,000 times) \e]4;1;#010203\x07\e]4;1;#030201\x07
expect: pal[1]=#030201
overrides: pal[1]
cite: overrides are a fixed table (256 + 3 entries); no growth per sequence. Generated by the test
flags: security

### OZ03_huge_osc_is_ignored_not_answered
size: 24x80
step: feed (OSC 11 ; then 1,048,576 bytes of 'a', then BEL)
reply: none
expect: bg=#101010
cite: a long spec is malformed (D-SPEC) and never echoed; the parser's unbounded OSC (ADR 0022) is a separate issue. Generated by the test
flags: security negative

### OZ04_reply_never_echoes_input
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;?;evil\x07\e]4;1;?;2;?;evil\x07
reply: \e]11;rgb:1010/1010/1010\x07\e]4;1;rgb:0101/fefe/5454\x07\e]4;2;rgb:0202/fdfd/5757\x07
cite: D-SECURITY (reports_spec.txt): replies are built from terminal state only, never from the program's bytes (`evil` is a bad spec for colour 12 / a lone index)
flags: security

### OZ05_invalid_utf8_in_spec_ignored
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;#ff\xff0000\x07
expect: bg=#101010
overrides: none
cite: D-SPEC: non-hex byte
flags: negative

### OZ06_nul_and_c0_removed_by_parser
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;#ff\x010000\x07
expect: bg=#ff0000
cite: ADR 0022 "Parser facts": C0 controls other than BEL, CAN, SUB and ESC are removed from the payload, so the spec is #ff0000
flags: decision

### OZ07_colour_sets_do_not_reply
size: 24x80
step: feed \e]11;#ff0000\x07\e]4;1;#00ff00\x07\e]104\x07\e]110\x07\e]111\x07\e]112\x07
